capture_method.name: ordered primary-source API capture, scholarly editorial-risk check, and source-visible scan review
capture_method.version: curl 8.18.0; Python 3.14.6; ToS bundled-DjVu parser v1

target: Exact German historical-edition witness for Der Antichrist beyond the provisional Russian collection expression

internet_archive_source_lineage.metadata_contamination_rationale: The current provider description is unrelated to the visible Nietzsche/Naumann 1906 Stanford scan and is not used for bibliographic identity or rights.

observations: Pages 1-2 visibly carry the Stanford University Libraries binding, bookplate, and barcode 36105025673729.
Page 5 visibly states Nietzsche's Werke, Erste Abtheilung, Band VIII, Leipzig, C. G. Naumann Verlag, 1906.
Page 6 visibly states 10. und 11. Tausend des Antichrist alongside separate printing statements for the other volume contents.
Pages 10-12 carry the volume contents; page 11 reports Vorwort at printed page 213 and Erstes Buch: Der Antichrist at printed page 215.
Page 228 begins Vorwort on printed page 213 and page 229 ends it on printed page 214.
Page 230 is the internal Der Antichrist title leaf; page 231 is a blank/furniture leaf; page 232 begins numbered section 1 on printed page 215.
Pages 254-261 visibly continue printed pages 239-246 within sections 22-26.
Pages 326-329 visibly continue printed pages 311-314; page 329 carries the terminal declaration after section 62.
Page 330 visibly begins Disposition und Entwürfe zum dritten Buch der Umwerthung aller Werthe; pages 331-332 continue that different section.
Pages 374-380 were checked as a negative boundary control and belong to later volume material, not Der Antichrist.
Pages 517-519 are publisher advertisements and pages 520-523 are rear binding and Stanford circulation furniture.

editorial_risk_evidence.source: Andreas Urs Sommer, Historischer und kritischer Kommentar zu Friedrich Nietzsches Werken, Band 6/2, 2013, Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften digital edition
editorial_risk_evidence.bounded_report: The commentary reports first publication in Koegel's 1895 volume, silent adoption of Köselitz corrections, and four suppressed passages. This makes the 1906 archive edition a historically important but editorially non-neutral witness.
